A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyGMamba. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original dynamic link prediction, node classification, ablation, and efficiency results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds experiments on three synthetic temporal-pattern datasets.

M1.justification: The two SSM blocks, patching, temporal-pattern-based information selection, predictor, and loss are retained. Corrected notation and dimensions, the Figure 1 label correction, and newly disclosed layer counts do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the seven real-world datasets and adds three seven-node synthetic graphs with increasing, decreasing, and periodic interaction intervals. These introduce distinct controlled temporal scenarios for link prediction (Section 4.2 and Appendix A.2).

E2.justification: Corresponding real-world benchmark, ablation, and efficiency comparisons retain their comparator membership. The new synthetic experiments use previously evaluated DyGFormer, CTAN, and Variant A; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: The synthetic experiments introduce a shared neighbor-count/patch-size search grid for DyGFormer and DyGMamba, with input length fixed at 32. Their chronological 70%/15%/15% splits ensure period starts occur in every S3 split. Existing real-world protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained real-world ablations and scalability analyses, v2 adds a controlled study of temporal-pattern modeling on S1–S3. Comparing DyGMamba with the existing time-level-SSM ablation, Variant A, directly tests that component under explicitly constructed temporal patterns (Table 5).

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with five random seeds and report means with error bars. v2's efficiency Table 15 caption reiterates that existing policy, and the synthetic results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports AP and AUC-ROC on S1–S3. For example, S1 AP is 81.58±1.31 for DyGMamba, 55.19±0.98 for DyGFormer, and 53.72±0.04 for Variant A. These are newly reported outcomes; matched real-world tables and existing scalability results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix A's detailed complexity derivation while retaining the verbal linear-versus-quadratic comparison in Section 4.3. It also corrects aggregation-weight dimensions to account for patch length in v2 Equations 7b/7d, corresponding to v1 Equations 8b/8d.

C1.justification: The abstract and scientific conclusion retain the same contribution: SSM-based CTDG modeling with temporal-pattern selection, strong link-prediction performance, and efficient long-history processing. Edits to the introduction's contribution list do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of the synthetic comparisons linking their performance advantage to temporal-pattern modeling, particularly through Variant A's similarity to DyGFormer. Appendix A.2 also explains why S3's split design requires periodic-pattern reasoning rather than merely learning increasing intervals.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies two layers in each SSM block and documents synthetic-data construction and tuning in Appendices A.2/C.2 and Table 11. Its conclusion also states that code is supplied as supplementary material; the supplied PDFs do not verify that availability.

R1.justification: v2 removes several references, including the graph-Mamba works by Wang et al. and Behrouz and Hashemi, and deletes their discussion alongside the explicit comparison with Li et al.'s DTDG SSM work. The main positioning against DyGFormer and CTAN remains.

P1.justification: v2 tightens motivation and method explanations, edits grammar and notation, combines evaluation and implementation descriptions, and reorganizes appendix subsections. Author affiliations and correspondence information change, and acknowledgments are removed; the main narrative structure remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from a 3-by-4 to a compact 2-by-6 scatterplot arrangement with green background shading, and Figure 4 changes aspect ratio. v2 adds synthetic Tables 5, 7, 8, and 11 plus Figure 5, alongside caption and diagram-label corrections. The earlier Figure 5 is retained as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The synthetic study provides more targeted evidence for temporal-pattern modeling than v1's real-world ablations alone, while the added layer counts and construction/tuning details help reproducibility. These constitute a limited net gain: existing benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and v2 loses the detailed complexity derivation and relevant graph-SSM related-work context.
